findings.reason: §2's line about dispositions is what tells the worker whether to extend `DIMENSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS` or invent a parallel space; as written it does neither and misnames the mechanism it cites.
findings.text: §2 says "the three dispositions `crew dispose` already records" and names them as a section, a fold into the node's next prompt, and an exemption, but the closed set is `DIMENSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("folded", "exempted")` — two kinds, written through `crew_dispose` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:565`), whose docstring states the same two ("a fold naming the dispatched node …, or an exemption naming why"). "A section" is not a recorded disposition at all; adopting it would add a third member to a closed set the plan never mentions. If the implementer takes the plan's wording at face value the new disposition is invented instead of the existing two extended.

findings.reason: naming the existing predicate turns §4 from a new check into a case added to the one predicate the plan store already routes every authored body through, and names the established refusal/warning pairing to copy. The review's own rubric also exists to catch a rebuild of present machinery, which is exactly what an uncited parallel scan is.
findings.text: §4 names `reckon/_store.py` and `reckon/_store_section_ops.py` as write paths but nowhere cites the mechanism those two files already share: `_forged_plan_structure` / `_refuse_forged_body_structure` (`reckon/_store.py:899,924`), whose own docstring says it exists because "Three sites write an authored body into plan HTML … and all three must refuse the same fragments … One predicate keeps the three from drifting apart", and which `reckon/_store_section_ops.py:124` `_refuse_forged_structure` imports precisely so its path "refuses exactly the fragments `insert_section` and `append_evidence` refuse". §4 must say it extends that predicate; a term scan written beside it is a fourth, drifting check. The refusal-plus-read-warning pattern §4 proposes is also already in the tree at `reckon/_store.py:667` `_unparsed_section_warnings` ("The write path refuses the splice; this read-time warning is its partner"), which the plan does not cite as its precedent.

findings.reason: the plan should name the prose extractor to extend and say whether the store guard and the `audit-doc` warning share one scanner or are two, instead of leaving three implementations of "prose without `<code>`" to accrete.
findings.text: §4 requires the term to be refused in a body's prose but allowed inside `<code>`, and proposes to implement that scan in `reckon/_store.py` and to add a matching `audit-doc` warning in `reckon/doccheck.py`. Both halves of that `<code>`-excluding prose read already have an owner this plan does not name: `reckon/doccheck.py:384` `_prose_text(el)` ("Visible text with the verbatim subtrees removed … Text inside `<pre>` and `<code>` renders literally, so an asterisk pair there is the subject a document is quoting"), and `reckon/_plan_html.py:474` `section_prose`, described at its caller `reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py:161` as "the one reader the review digests and the …" and used at seven call sites (`mcp_views.py:2116,2256`, `dispatch_sections.py:202`, `plan_review.py:338,705,2357`). A third, independently written `<code>`-stripping regex will disagree with those, and two implementations means they can drift silently — which is the exact failure `_forged_plan_structure`'s docstring names.

findings.reason: §1 states the term is purged from every reckon surface; without these two paths named, the purge completes with the term still in `reckon/` and nothing reports it, and a worker cannot add a path the brief does not grant.
findings.text: census of production sites carrying the term that appear in no section's write-path list. §1's census says the term lives in 19 production files, and the sections between them name every one except two: `reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:131` ("landing line, a checkpoint or a follow-on naming another session's") and `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:126` ("discarded run that reached main through a follow-on"). Both are module comments naming the term rather than code, which is why they fall between §2's list (review/repair/findings/reports) and §3's (prompts/ledger-carried key readers) — §2 grants "other test files the change breaks … from the failure ids the worker reports", but §5's prose sweep is scoped to `skills/` alone, so a comment-only site in `reckon/` reaches neither list and no gate fails on it.

findings.reason: the item exists to make a section account for the interface it adds; §4 is the only section that adds a refusal and it is the only one that accounts for none, so the accounting is presently impossible to check.
findings.text: counted refusal_families 23 (the counter reads "distinct literal family codes passed to `format_refusal`", `reckon/interface_counts.py:30`), yet §4 adds a refusal surface in the plan store and a new `audit-doc` warning kind and says nothing about what either retires, merges, or joins. The section must state whether the refusal is a new family code or an existing one, and what warning kind the `audit-doc` case reuses or replaces.

findings.reason: a section that adds a member to a closed set must name what it retires or merges, or say why nothing can; as written the added kind arrives unaccounted for and the reader cannot tell it from the existing exemptions.
findings.text: §2 lands a disposition kind that does not exist ("a section") alongside the two `crew dispose` records, which adds a member to the closed `DIMENSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS` tuple (`reckon/crew/review.py:3426`) and therefore to the interface, while §2's prose accounts only for the severity rename.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; §3 removes the promotion conversion rather than layering over it, and §4's guard lands inside `reckon/_store.py`, the deep owner of plan writes already reached by `_store_section_ops`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's `<code>`-excluding term scan duplicates prose extraction already owned elsewhere, and a census of the term's production sites shows two files carrying it under no section's write paths.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2014, cli_options 400, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23; §4 adds a store refusal and an `audit-doc` warning kind, and §2 adds a third disposition kind to a closed two-kind set, with neither section naming what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 misstates the closed set `crew dispose` already records, and §4 proposes a plan-body term guard without citing `reckon/_store.py`'s existing single body predicate `_forged_plan_structure` / `_refuse_forged_body_structure` that every authoring path already routes through.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the three mechanism changes are renames (§2 severities, §3 manifest field and ledger key) and one deletion (§3's followup conversion); nothing in the plan forwards to existing machinery behind a thinner interface.
